ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepFun.statement: Let $\Omega$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be measurable spaces. For functions $f : \Omega \to \alpha$, $g : \Omega \to \beta$, $h : \Omega \to \gamma$ and a measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ (an automatically supplied argument), $\mathrm{CondIndepFun}\ f\ g\ h\ \mu$ is the proposition that for almost every $z \in \gamma$ with respect to the pushforward measure $h_*\mu$, the functions $f$ and $g$ are independent (`IndepFun`) with respect to the conditional measure $\mu[\,\cdot \mid h^{-1}(\{z\})]$, i.e. $\mu$ conditioned on the set $h^{-1}(\{z\})$. Per the docstring, this is the assertion that $f$ and $g$ are conditionally independent relative to $h$.
